extracted.intended_audience: computer vision and AI researchers, dataset creators, and model developers working on visual understanding and computational humor
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and using a dataset and evaluation suite to measure how well AI systems understand graphical humor (photos, cartoons, sketches, and AI-generated images), via classification, rating, and comparison tasks and associated analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controlled, carefully curated dataset
rubrics_metrics.description: HumorDB: a novel, controlled, and carefully curated dataset designed to evaluate and advance visual humor understanding by AI systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dataset curation should be deliberate and controlled to support targeted evaluation of visual humor; the paper emphasizes careful selection and curation to probe specific phenomena in humor understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity of image modalities
rubrics_metrics.description: The dataset comprises diverse images spanning photos, cartoons, sketches, and AI-generated content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include multiple modalities (real photos, cartoons, sketches, AI-generated) because different modalities present distinct challenges (e.g., abstraction in sketches). Evaluation should measure model performance across these modalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimally contrastive pairs
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes minimally contrastive pairs where subtle edits differentiate between humorous and non-humorous versions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use minimally contrastive pairs to test sensitivity to small, humor-critical edits; these pairs probe fine-grained contextual and relational understanding rather than broad pattern recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Binary humor classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate models on binary humor classification (is the image humorous or not).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This task provides a basic correctness metric; useful as a coarse measure of whether models can detect humor at all.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funniness rating prediction
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate models on funniness rating prediction (predicting a continuous or ordinal funniness score).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This captures graded judgments about how funny an image is and can be formulated as regression or ordinal prediction; useful to measure nuance beyond binary labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pairwise humor comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate models on pairwise humor comparison (deciding which of two images is funnier).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pairwise comparisons probe relative judgment and can be more robust to calibration differences across annotators or models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human baseline and gap-to-human analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate humans, state-of-the-art vision models, and large vision-language models on the tasks; results reveal a gap between current AI systems and human-level humor understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use human performance as the gold standard; quantify gaps to identify where models fail relative to humans and prioritize research directions accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Per-modality performance and weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Pretrained vision-language models perform better than vision-only models but still struggle with abstract sketches and subtle humor cues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report and analyze performance broken down by modality (e.g., sketches vs photos) and by cue subtlety; identifying modality-specific weaknesses is essential for targeted improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attention / region-focus alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis of attention maps shows that even when models correctly classify humorous images, they often fail to focus on the precise regions that make the image funny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate where models attend (attention maps, saliency) and measure alignment between model focus and the regions humans identify as humor-critical; lack of alignment signals spurious or shallow reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanistic interpretability and explanation evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary mechanistic interpretability studies and evaluation of model explanations provide initial insights into how different architectures process humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include interpretability analyses and explicit evaluation of model explanations to understand mechanisms behind model judgments and to diagnose failure modes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for contextual and abstract reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: An effective understanding of visual humor requires sophisticated architectures capable of detecting subtle contextual features and bridging the gap between visual perception and abstract reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design evaluations and model diagnostics that assess contextual reasoning and abstract inference (relations, social/pragmatic knowledge) in addition to perceptual capabilities; emphasize architectures and training that integrate perception with higher-level reasoning.
